candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — iron-status monitoring during epoetin alfa therapy
candidate.educational_objective: Maintain adequate iron stores during epoetin alfa therapy for CKD-related anemia because iron deficiency can impair the erythropoietic response.

options.A: Evaluate iron status and maintain adequate iron repletion because iron deficiency can limit the erythropoietic response to epoetin alfa.
options.B: Stop assessing iron status once epoetin alfa is started because the medication provides the iron needed for red blood cell production.
options.C: Monitor iron only when the client is receiving oral iron because intravenous or supplemental iron needs are unrelated to epoetin alfa response.
options.D: Avoid correcting iron deficiency because adequate iron stores reduce the effectiveness of erythropoiesis-stimulating therapy.

candidate.rationale: Current EPOGEN prescribing information instructs clinicians to evaluate iron status in all patients before and during treatment and to maintain iron repletion. Iron deficiency is a recognized cause of inadequate hemoglobin response to epoetin alfa, and many patients with CKD require supplemental iron during erythropoiesis-stimulating-agent therapy. Epoetin alfa stimulates erythropoiesis but does not supply iron. Therefore, A is correct. B and C incorrectly stop or restrict iron monitoring, and D reverses the relationship between iron deficiency and treatment response.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports iron-status assessment and maintenance of iron repletion before and during epoetin alfa therapy and identifies iron deficiency as a cause of inadequate treatment response.
